title: ASB length mi->km defect (19 Iraq gas rows) — TWO families, TWO different one-cell fixes
summary: OPEC's ASB length column is headed '(miles)' but the IRAQ block is tabulated in KILOMETRES, and the ingest converted anyway, so 19 rows are 1.609x too long. Route geometry arbitrates 6-0 for the raw figure. The fixes DIFFER by family: 13 rows (P18xx/P22xx) hold the converted km in LengthKnown with units 'km' -> correct the NUMBER; 6 rows (P40xx) hold the ASB integer verbatim with units 'mi' -> correct ONLY the UNIT LABEL, never the number (changing both would double-correct, and pasting the computed LengthKnownKm would silently revert on the next recalc). Iraq-and-Libya only: Qatar/Saudi/UAE blocks are genuine miles and a blanket sweep would corrupt them. OPEC never fixed Iraq (ASB2017 reprints the same integers), so any re-ingest reintroduces this. Independently corroborated: an Iraqi MoO Director General's own 2013 figure (~2,307 km) sits +66% below GEM as-is, +21% after this fix, and -6% after also removing P4061's double count.

title: CapacityUnits mislabelled on 3 Iraq rows — and the screen says it is tracker-wide
summary: P7477 (130 MMcf/d tagged bcm/y, ~98x HIGH), P4041 (258 MMSCFD tagged MMSCMD, ~35x HIGH) and P1841 (2.41 bcm/y tagged MMcf/d, ~120x LOW) each store a CORRECT number under a WRONG unit label. The directions differ, so this is careless per-row tagging, not one systematic conversion -- there is no blanket fix. It is not cosmetic: P7477's 22 km 18-inch spur is currently the SECOND-LARGEST-CAPACITY ROW IN ALL OF GGIT (130.00 bcm/y, ahead of the 14,202 km Texas Eastern) and P4041 is 8th, so every Iraq and global capacity total is distorted. A diameter-based screen over 1,964 GGIT rows finds a WORSE non-Iraqi row -- P2009 Mountaineer (US), 4,750 MMcf/d on an 8-inch 5.5 km lateral, 157x its ceiling -- plus P0693 Frigg UK at 31x, so DO NOT close this as an Iraq item. Three one-cell edits here; a tracker-wide pass is a separate task (normalise Diameter units first -- P2459 holds 1420 mm in an inches column).

title: P6824 is a DIESEL pipeline in the gas tracker (Arabic 'زيت الغاز' false friend)
summary: P6824 'Shouibah-Khor Al-Zubair' is a gas oil (diesel) EXPORT line: its own al-Mirbad ref says 'أنبوب تصدير زيت الغاز' and matches GEM on every spec (46 km, 8-10in, Shuaiba -> Khor al-Zubair OIL port, Oil Pipelines Company, completed July 2024). 'زيت الغاز' is literally 'gas oil' = diesel, not natural gas -- the row is perfectly sourced and completely misfiled, with no internal inconsistency to catch it. REMOVE from GGIT and refer to GOIT; do not merely re-label Fuel. Second country with this exact class after Libya's three condensate lines -- recommend a tracker-wide screen for GGIT rows whose source describes a liquid (port/berth/refinery destinations, sub-12in with the word 'export', Arabic 'المكثفات'/'زيت الغاز').

title: ASB provenance ruling — 12 of 16 duplicate/existence flags WITHDRAWN (my own earlier legs were wrong)
summary: The OPEC ASB gas table is a PER-PIPELINE table, not an aggregate, so 8 'single-sourced, existence unproven' flags rested on a false premise: the 13-row crosswalk matches diameter 13/13 and capacity 10/13, clinched by 'Baiji-K3-/Al Kaem' -> 'Baiji-K3-Al Kaem Gas Pipeline' with the doubled hyphen surviving verbatim. Two more flags were url_verifier large-PDF artefacts (the Kabesa and Najaf tokens ARE in the PDF). And the 'Strategic-* vs Trans-Iraq(i)-*' duplicate theory is refuted BY the source: ASB2017 lists both families as separate rows off different trunks to DIFFERENT power stations (Hilla vs Hilla-2, Al-Najaf 23/16in vs Najaf 74/24in) -- GEM's ingest merely TRUNCATED 'Hilla-2' to 'Hilla'. Staged a rename, not a merge. What survives: ONE real duplicate (P4054 -> merge into P4066) and ONE open aggregate/segment question (cluster C below). Single-sourcing is still a real weakness; unproven existence is not.

title: Cluster C — P4061 national 42-inch trunk vs P1852 segment: a 600 km double count
summary: P4061 'National dry gas' (600 km, 42in, 8.69 bcm/y) appears to aggregate P1852 (470 km, 42in, 11.03 bcm/y) rather than sit beside it. The tell is that the putative TRUNK carries LOWER capacity than its putative SEGMENT, which is physically backwards -- the same signature as Libya's cluster-A coastal double count. Independently supported by the aggregate test: removing P4061's 600 km is what takes GEM's Iraq operating total from +21% to -6% of the Iraqi MoO DG's own published figure. Needs the same ruling shape as Libya cluster A: either delete the member, or move P4061 to a PipelineNetworkGrouping label with a BLANK Status (note 'n/a' is not a valid Status). Both rows are staged as 'concern', tier medium -- neither is confirmed a duplicate on evidence alone.

title: Cluster B — P4054 is a third naming of P4066 (the one confirmed duplicate)
summary: P4054 duplicates P4066 (Trans-Iraq dry gas -> Daura power station, 29 mi/18in in ASB2017). Merge P4054 INTO P4066, carrying any unique names to OtherEnglishNames. This is the only genuine duplicate to survive the provenance ruling above, so it is a clean, low-risk action -- but it needs a ruling because a merge deletes a published ProjectID.

title: RETRACTED — P4067 is NOT a crude line misfiled in GGIT. Do not remove it (a standing country-note finding is wrong).
summary: STOP BEFORE ACTING ON THIS ONE. docs/country_notes/iraq.md has carried, since the 2026-07-07 ref-harvest re-pass, the finding 'P4067 (Al-Ahdab-Al-Zubaydia) is crude oil -> belongs in GOIT, not GGIT', source-backed by Iraq Business News and BBC Arabic establishing that Al-Ahdab is a crude-oil FIELD. The premise is true; the conclusion does not follow, and acting on it would delete a legitimate GGIT row. Inferring a pipeline's fluid from its source field's principal product is invalid: an oil field produces associated gas, this line's destination is a POWER STATION ('Al-Zubaydia PWR St'), and an oil-field-to-power-plant gas line is the most ordinary object in Iraq's gas network -- Majnoon, Gharraf, Faiha, West Qurna and Buzergan rows are all that shape. Decisively, OPEC lists the Ahdab corridor's crude and gas lines as SEPARATE rows in SEPARATE tables of the same publication: ASB2017 Table 6.9 (crude) 'Ahdeb/Wassit P P (2) OPC 42, 45 16, 10' and Table 9.9 (gas) 'Al-Ahdeb/Al-Zubaydia PWR St OPC 73 16' -- which is the opposite of a mis-filing. I reached the same wrong conclusion independently earlier in this pass, so this corrects both readings. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: Al-Jibawi reports a genuinely NEW 16-inch / 76 km CRUDE line from Ahdab to Zubaidiya completed in early 2024 -- a GOIT DISCOVERY CANDIDATE, not a GGIT removal. A 2016-vintage OPEC gas table cannot contain a line finished in 2024, so these are two different pipes on one corridor. Residual uncertainty stated plainly: both share a 16-inch diameter and a 73-76 km length, so it cannot be fully excluded that one line is being described twice with different fluids -- flagged for a human read, not asserted. BONUS: Al-Jibawi's independent 76 km is the first SOURCE-STATED confirmation of the ASB mi->km length defect on any of its 19 rows (the sheet computes 117.48 km on this row). The guard this implies for the tracker-wide liquids screen recommended in the gasoil memo: key on what the source says the PIPE CARRIES, never on what its origin field produces.

title: A pipeline's LENGTH was populated from a 'X km from' DISTANCE statement (P7457) — a second length-provenance class
summary: RETRACTION FIRST: an earlier entry here said 'P7457 Semel-Duhok has ZERO verifiable sources.' That was WRONG. The KRG Ministry of Natural Resources documents the line twice (an archived gas-pipelines page and the 26 May 2014 'First Gas Arrives at Duhok Power Station' release), with Iraq Business News, DNO and OGJ corroborating -- five verifiable sources, two of them government primaries. Status operating, StartYear1 2014 and Capacity 120 MMcf/d are all now CONFIRMED, and DNO's '100 MMcf/d' turns out to be the ramp-up figure ('starting at around 55mmscf/d, ramping up to 120mmscf/d'), not a conflict. What replaces the retracted claim is a smaller but generalizable defect: MNR states the PIPELINE is '30-kilometre', while GEM holds 40.00 km -- and 40 km is what DNO and OGJ both give as the DISTANCE from the field to the plant ('located 40 kilometers from the field'). A straight-line separation between two points was transcribed as a pipeline length. That is a distinct failure mode from the ASB mi->km defect and needs its own screen: it leaves no unit artefact, no round-number tell, and no internal inconsistency -- the number is simply about a different thing. Worth a ruling on whether to screen GGIT for LengthKnown values traceable to 'N km from/away' phrasing, especially on short field-to-plant interconnectors where the two figures differ by only tens of percent. Diameter 36in remains unsourced on this row and looks large for a 30 km 120 MMcf/d interconnector.

title: RETRACTED — 'status is stale FORWARD on 2 rows' (P7435, P6826). GEM was right both times.
summary: WITHDRAWN, and recorded rather than deleted so the packet is not applied against it. This pass staged Status 'operating' -> 'construction' on P7435 and P6826, arguing GEM was ahead of the evidence. Al-Jibawi (June 2025) refutes both: P7435 -- 'In February 2025, SCOP started to construct a 42-inch dry gas pipeline ... In May 2025, the Oil Minister, Hayan Al-Sawad, declared the completion of the pipeline in a record time'; P6826 -- OPC 'completed in 2024 the construction of a 24-inch dry gas pipeline extending for 8 km from the Majnoon oil field ... to the NGL station in North Rumaila'. The refs I relied on (Baghdad Today Feb-2025, Iraq Business News Mar-2025, al-Sharq Apr-2024) were quoted accurately; they simply dated the CONSTRUCTION PHASE of builds that finished weeks or months later. Al-Jibawi's February date matches Baghdad Today exactly, which is what makes its completion claim a continuation rather than a competing account. The methodological point is the reason this is escalated at all: before staging a 'stale forward' status change, look explicitly for a LATER source -- on short lines 'under construction' can be ten weeks from 'operating', so construction-stage reporting is weak evidence against an operating flag and should never carry a change on its own. TWO SIDE-EFFECTS, both improvements: Al-Jibawi also resolves the al-Sharq route contradiction on P6826 (Majnoon -> North Rumaila NGL, so GEM's name is right and the two al-Sharq statements describe one corridor from opposite ends), and it confirms 40 km/42in on P7435 and 8 km/24in on P6826 exactly. WHAT SURVIVES: P6826's StartYear1 is 2024, not 2025 -- one cell, sourced -- and P7435's blank StartYear1 can be filled 2025-05. No ruling needed; the two proposed status edits are already withdrawn from the staged JSON.

title: P7436/P7437 owner is TotalEnergies' project, not the Ministry of Oil
summary: Both rows carry Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil [100.%]' against a single ref that never mentions the Ministry: the Artawi GMP EPSCC Project is 'commissioned by TotalEnergies', with China Petroleum Pipeline Engineering as EPC contractor. Do NOT simply swap in TotalEnergies at 100% -- Ratawi/Artawi is a consortium, so establish the real split from a primary source first, and record it on the ProjectID-keyed operators/owners tab (GID 1489950650). The same ref DOES support both rows' specs exactly (83 km/20in and 114 km/26in sour gas), so only the ownership is wrong. Note the two rows also share an identical PipelineName with no SegmentName, which will read as a duplicate to any future name-based pass.

title: GulfPub<->GEM matching is unreliable for Iraq — do NOT act on its conflict list
summary: The >10% conflict gate tripped numerically (13 of 39 = 33%) but NOT materially: zero of the 13 conflicts sit on a green match (all yellow, composite 0.455-0.653; the run produced only 4 green matches out of 39 overlaps) and matches collapse many-to-one. These are matching artefacts, not data disagreements. Recorded so the gate is not re-tripped and re-investigated next scrape. Genuine referrals were split out separately to batches/iraq-gas/staging/recon-gulfpub-followup/ (Mansuriyah-Kirkuk, Jera Pika-Mansuriyah).

title: url_verifier.py false negatives cost 33 of 41 'dead' refs — six families, two new
summary: The ref-gap re-pass, plus the Leg-3 research that followed it, leaves only 8 of 41 DEAD_LINK units with no usable source. 31 recovered and 2 more turned out to have LIVE urls whose content CONTRADICTS the GEM value -- a worse problem than a dead link, and invisible while the unit was written off as dead. Nearly every substantive defect in this packet (P6824 diesel, P7477 capacity, P7436/P7437 owner, P6827's 43-year date error, P6826's StartYear1, P7457's length) was found in a ref that had been marked dead, and two findings I staged off recovered refs were then REFUTED by a further recovered ref (P7435/P6826 status -- see the retraction entry), which cuts both ways: recovery is where the yield is AND where the over-reading risk is. Families: large PDFs the verifier cannot read deep enough (saymar 4.2 MB, Al-Jibawi, both ASB editions -- this family alone carried most of the pass's confirmations); CAPTCHA interstitials returning HTTP 200 with a 2,654-byte / 267-character body (opc.oil.gov.iq, the correct primary source for P7471/P7474, so the fix is access not replacement); bot-wall 403 with no archive (pukmedia); Facebook permalinks returning 400 to non-browser clients; Wayback replay truncating large files at exactly 5 MiB, leaving an unparseable PDF (qamarenergy, which is why P6823's capacity stays unsourced); and NEW -- hosts that intermittently ConnectTimeout while genuinely reachable (mnr.krg.org answered, then timed out minutes later), where the fix is to cite a Wayback snapshot for stability rather than to conclude the source is gone. Note P7457 shows that a genuinely unrecoverable ref does not imply an unsourceable ROW: both its cited urls stayed dead, yet five other sources including two KRG government primaries were found. Recommended verifier changes: never emit DEAD_LINK on a 2xx response; retry large PDFs with a ranged fetch; and retry timeouts once before failing.
